analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation only: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (new paragraph near head lines 549-567) and docs/architecture/inference.md (scheduler geometry table, new 'Prompt geometry' section, invariants 8 and 9). No executable code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, authorization or encryption path changes. The docs describe a provider behavior change, not made in this diff, that gives Gemma 4 a wider default prefill chunk of 2048 with a 4096 step budget. Bidirectional media keeps 512. GPT-OSS, dense Qwen and other families keep 512/2048.

Threat-model relevance is limited to availability and memory-admission (T-010, T-029 and the TB-007 inference engine boundary). The docs claim the paged pool is sized from max(prefillChunk, stripe), which is unchanged at 2048, so KV grants and the load quotation do not move. They also claim a Gemma peak of 3.73 GiB against the 5.5 GiB activation reserve. Those figures rest on a cited measurement report and on source (EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift, SchedulerV2) that were not supplied, so I cannot confirm them. A consumer-controlled workload, such as many concurrent long prompts, could exceed the activation reserve if the claims are wrong. That would be a provider-local OOM or availability concern, not a confirmed regression. The docs note the p99 inter-token gap grows 2-3x, which is a latency tradeoff, not a security issue.

Invariants 8 and 9 describe a runtime guard that raises max(chunk, stripe) to 1,120 tokens and a rule that media chunks never exceed the ring size. The implementing code is not in this batch. The next pass should verify the code for the following: the DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK override bounds, the media block-size validation that keeps a media block within maxPrefillChunk, and that the override disqualifies reviewed profiles. No prefix-cache T-041 behavior (at-rest crypto, HMAC naming, TTL) is touched. I identified no new attack surface or threat-model invalidation from the docs alone.
